question: A single charity's coin collection started the month with 117 dollars. The total was split evenly among 3 collection boxes, and this story follows just one box. A matching sponsor then multiplied that box's total by 7. A large withdrawal for event costs then cost the box 103 dollars. A late donation added 13 more dollars. Finally, a year-end match multiplied the box's total by 5. How much money was in that one box in the end?

A photographer had 199 photos. They doubled the count (multiplied by 2) through digital enhancement. They added 63 more photos from a shoot. They multiplied by 6 for batch processing. They added 45 photos for album finalization. A competitor had 500 photos but didn't contribute. Using a word quantity, twice her original amount—how many photos after doubling and adding the shoot, but before multiplication?

A vineyard had 185 crates of grapes, tracked over 120 minutes, or 2 hours, of the harvest, even though the vineyard has 30 acres. Eight more matching vineyards joined a co-op, making the total nine times as large. A shipment removed 1,197 crates for a spoiled batch. Four more matching vineyards joined, making the total five times as large. Finally, four more matching vineyards joined again, making it five times as large. How many crates of grapes did the co-op end up with?

A garden had 50 tomato plants. They multiplied by 5 for spring planting. They added 69 plants from the nursery. They multiplied by 3 for the total garden expansion. They removed 578 plants for a market sale. They removed another 14 plants that wilted. What was the final count of tomato plants?

A charity tracked the total dollars in its bake sale cash box, starting with 25 dollars in starting change. A morning sale added 29 more dollars. A refund for a burnt batch removed 43 dollars. An afternoon sale added 18 more dollars. A dozen volunteers ran the booth that day, though that number has nothing to do with the cash total. Converting the tracked total into a token-count for the raffle — a simple unit change — the total was tripled. A matching sponsor then tripled the tracked token count once more. How many tokens did the tracked total come to?

A student started with 69 points. She added 29 points from morning test. She subtracted 80 points from errors. She added 36 points from corrections. She subtracted 29 points from recalculation. She added 63 points from bonus (measured in total adjusted points). Throughout testing, morning questions, afternoon sections, and evening review tracked progress through one continuous quantity. His exam score was 14 points higher (separate tracking). What was the final adjusted point total?
A store starts with 32 items. It divides by 4 (8). It loses 3 (5). It loses 3 (2). It adds 80 (82). It divides by 2 (41). Half of 8 is 4. How many remain?

A library had 135 books (starting catalog). They divided by 3 for branch distribution (morning). They added 72 from donations (mid-morning). They subtracted 115 for archiving (afternoon). They added 6 final books (evening). Two managers tracked it (named: Manager A vs B). After division but before additions, how many books in the early morning state?

Grace had 110 dollars saved, more than her brother Sam's 30. She earned 53 more dollars babysitting. She then spent 156 dollars on a new phone case and screen protector bundle. A refund program tripled whatever cash she had left. A final bonus from her part-time job multiplied it eightfold. How much money did Grace have in the end?

A camp had 109 packets of soup and used 99 of them during the first week. Every packet still in the cupboard makes 8 bowls. A parent donated 38 ready-made bowls of soup for the weekend. The hikers ate 74 bowls on Saturday. A late delivery added 3 more bowls that evening. The camp sleeps 60 people. How many bowls of soup are there now?

Early on Saturday morning Ines picked 122 plums from the tree behind her house and kept half of them, sending the rest round to her neighbour. Before lunch she used 33 of her own plums to make a pot of jam. In the early afternoon a friend arrived with 27 plums from his garden for her. Later that afternoon she sold 47 plums at the roadside table by the gate. In the evening her daughter came home with 5 more from the market. The price card on the roadside table is written in cents rather than dollars. How many plums does Ines have at the end of the day?

A beekeeper had 55 frames of honeycomb ready in the spring. He mentioned a dozen new gloves were ordered for the season, though that had nothing to do with the honeycomb count. A strong nectar flow turned every frame into 8 frames. A second hive added 56 more frames. A record harvest then turned every frame into 5 frames. A wholesale buyer then purchased 1898 frames in one large order. How many frames of honeycomb were left after the wholesale order?
A supplier had 97 units initially. This was multiplied by 5. Then multiplied by 6. This was divided by 2. He removed 92. A partner warehouse had 58 units. What was the final total?

A storage facility had 182 boxes initially. They removed 155 through clearance. They added 7 new boxes. Then 42 more arrived. Finally, 63 additional boxes were received. They removed 119 for moving out. A warehouse facility had 1000 boxes but separate location. How many boxes remain in storage?

A car wash began the day with 176 dollars earned, multiplied across 7 identical stations, each earning that same amount, for the week's total. A tip jar added 8 more dollars. Unrelated to the car wash, a nearby gas station sold 200 gallons of fuel that same day. A bonus added 11 more dollars. Since the shop records earnings in dollars but the franchise report lists cents, the manager always converted the numbers. A matching program made the total grow to 4 times its size. How much money did the car wash have after that program?
A class had 108 students morning. Added 70. Multiplied by 5 groupwork. Multiplied by 3 larger event. Added 61 afternoon. What is afternoon attendance?

On Monday morning Ines counted 133 bags of compost in the garden centre yard, and her colleague Dmitri wheeled in 64 more, though Ines shifts more bags in a day than Dmitri does. By lunchtime 170 bags had been sold to landscapers. In the afternoon head office arranged for each of its 7 regional yards to hold the same number of bags as this yard, and that became the whole regional stock. That evening 76 bags were loaded onto a lorry for a golf course. A late cancellation brought 40 bags back into the regional stock. How many bags of compost were in the regional stock at the end of the day?

On Monday morning a florist had 71 stems of lilies. Before lunch 44 stems were used in bouquets, and in the early afternoon 3 stems wilted and were thrown away. Later that afternoon the florist cut every remaining stem into 3 short sprigs for table decorations. In the evening 1 sprig was dropped on the floor and 3 more were given to a customer. The shop closes at 6. How many sprigs does the florist have?

At a cereal factory that has run for a dozen years, Rafa fills each box with 165 grams of flakes and Tam adds 63 grams of nuts, so Rafa puts more into every box than Tam does. The boxes are packed 9 to a carton, the cartons 6 to a pallet, and the pallets 9 to a truck. The factory employs 40 workers. Today 8 full trucks left the loading dock. How many grams of cereal left the factory today?

A group had 131 members initially. They added 11 new members. Then 65 more joined. They added 12 additional recruits. Finally, 69 more members signed up. A large organization had 1000 members but different affiliation. How many total group members?

Xu's cafe sells 75 cups of coffee each morning and twice that many cups over the whole day. On top of the coffees, the cafe sells 29 pots of tea each day. Xu's cafe is open 7 days a week, and the festival season lasts 3 weeks with the same sales every day. How many drinks does the cafe sell during the festival season?
A worker started with 191 units. She removed 185. This was multiplied by 8. This was divided by 6. This was divided by 4. Measured in hours (time conversion), how many?

A farmer started with 175 animals. By morning, 93 were sold to a market. He then added 57 new animals from breeding. The total multiplied by 4. After disease, 487 animals were lost (representing a painful week). The remainder multiplied by 3. Finally, 56 animals were removed for a sanctuary transfer. A neighboring farm had 1000 animals but separate location. How many animals remain on the farm?

Fenna keeps a sourdough starter that weighs 87 grams, more than the 80 grams of starter her friend Gus keeps. She uses 85 grams of it in a loaf. She then feeds what is left with flour and water until it weighs 8 times as much. The next day she feeds it again until it weighs 8 times as much as before. Her oven bakes at 230 degrees. Finally she divides the starter into 2 equal portions and keeps only 1 portion in the jar. How many grams of starter are in Fenna's jar now?

A warehouse tracked morning, afternoon, and evening movement. Starting with 134 boxes, morning deliveries added 80 (214 boxes). Afternoon shipments added 59 (273 boxes). Outgoing orders removed 182 (91 boxes). Evening preparation multiplied by 3 (273 boxes). Tomorrow's projection multiplied by 6. Converting to dozens, this represented about 137 dozen boxes. What was tomorrow's projection?
